financials_interim.notes: Licensed finance company (NBFI, Muthoot Group subsidiary) -- single entity, no Group/Company split (the filing itself only presents 'Company' columns, no subsidiaries). Verified via both EPS figures: basic 3.46 = 429,411,257 / 124,195,533 ordinary shares; diluted 2.42 = 429,411,257 / 177,544,130 adjusted weighted-average shares (including convertible irredeemable preference shares) -- both match exactly, no extraction issues. revenue = Total revenue per the segmental analysis note (p.9), = interest income + other income (3,566,710,844); operating_profit = 'Operating Profit before Value Added Tax on Financial Services' (1,158,873,536), the company's own subtotal before the VAT-FS levy that sits between it and PBT. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables left blank -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split disclosed; 'Financial assets at amortized cost - Loans and advances' (50,508,715,546) is the core earning asset, not a trade receivable. long_term_borrowings = 'Other borrowed funds' (19,410,647,586) + 'Debenture' (2,758,098,373) = 22,168,745,959, both genuine interest-bearing debt (debenture detail on p.11). short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks' (6,954,352) only. 'Due to Customers' (30,374,074,594, deposits) is deliberately excluded from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt in the conventional sense. Cash flow figures are for the quarter in isolation (p.8), but the filing's own comparative column for cash flow is the FULL YEAR ended 31 March 2026, not the prior Q1 -- so no YoY cash-flow comparison is possible from this filing, only the current quarter's absolute figures are entered. capex = acquisition of PPE (103,597,471) + prepayments for right-of-use assets (3,480,000) = 107,077,471 (no intangible asset acquisitions this quarter).

interim_updates.note_text: Asia Asset Finance (AAF), a Muthoot Group NBFI, delivered a very strong Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026): PBT Rs.877.9mn (+197.8% YoY) and PAT Rs.429.4mn (+137.0% YoY). Interest income grew 85.4% YoY to Rs.3.40bn and net interest income nearly doubled (+120.0%) to Rs.1.97bn, driven by loan portfolio growth to Rs.50.51bn (+Rs.3.51bn during the quarter alone) and total assets reaching Rs.60.42bn (+12.3% quarter-on-quarter). Per the company's own segmental disclosure, growth was broad-based across all three lending segments YoY: Gold Loan segment result +195% (Rs.276.8mn to Rs.816.4mn, the largest absolute contributor), Loans and advances segment result +100% (Rs.107.4mn to Rs.215.2mn), and Finance lease segment result +883% off a small base (Rs.9.6mn to Rs.94.5mn). Asset quality improved materially alongside the growth: Gross NPA ratio fell from 12.5% to 7.5% and Net NPA ratio from 6.6% to 4.2%. Return on Equity (annualised) rose to 34.4% (from 18.7%) and Return on Assets (annualised) to 3.0% (from 1.8%). Capital ratios remain comfortably above regulatory minimums (Tier 1 18.96% vs 8.5% minimum) though they softened YoY (from 24.07%) as the balance sheet grew faster than the capital base. The company opened 5 new branches during the quarter (120 branches total) and a new training centre in Kurunegala.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for AAF -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. The filing's cash flow statement compares the quarter only against the FULL YEAR ended 31 March 2026, not a prior quarter, so no YoY or QoQ cash-flow comparison is possible; only the current quarter's absolute cash flow figures are stored.
interim_updates.takeaway: A genuinely strong, broad-based quarter -- growth, profitability, and asset quality all improved together rather than trading off against each other, which is the more demanding combination for an NBFI. The Gold Loan segment is the single largest driver of the profit increase, worth watching given gold-price sensitivity, but Loans & Advances and Finance Lease both grew strongly too. Capital ratios softening (still well above minimums) simply reflects the balance sheet growing faster than retained capital, not a capital-quality issue.
operational_highlights: PBT Rs.877.9mn (+197.8% YoY), PAT Rs.429.4mn (+137.0% YoY); EPS Rs.3.46 (from Rs.1.46)
Net interest income nearly doubled YoY (+120.0%) to Rs.1.97bn; loan portfolio grew Rs.3.51bn during the quarter alone to Rs.50.51bn; total assets Rs.60.42bn (+12.3% QoQ)
Asset quality improved materially: Gross NPA ratio 12.5% to 7.5%; Net NPA ratio 6.6% to 4.2%
Return on Equity (annualised) 34.4% (from 18.7%); Return on Assets (annualised) 3.0% (from 1.8%); Net Interest Margin (annualised) 13.9% (from 10.6%)
Capital remains well above regulatory minimums (Tier 1 18.96% vs 8.5% min; Total Capital 18.85% vs 12.5% min) but softened YoY (from 24.07%/23.89%) as the balance sheet grew faster than capital

Opened 5 new branches during the quarter (120 branches total) and a new staff training centre in Kurunegala; recommended a final dividend of Rs.0.57/ordinary share and Rs.0.70/preference share for FY2025/26
key_drivers: By segment (YoY, per the company's own segmental note): Gold Loan segment result +195% (Rs.276.8mn to Rs.816.4mn) -- the largest absolute contributor to PBT growth; Loans and advances segment +100% (Rs.107.4mn to Rs.215.2mn); Finance lease segment +883% off a small base (Rs.9.6mn to Rs.94.5mn)

Net interest margin expansion (10.6% to 13.9% annualised) combined with strong volume growth (loan book +7.5% quarter-on-quarter alone) drove net interest income growth well above interest income growth (120% vs 85%), indicating funding-cost discipline alongside asset growth

Improving asset quality (Gross NPA 12.5% to 7.5%) alongside rapid loan growth is the more demanding combination for an NBFI than either alone -- worth continuing to monitor as growth continues, though the trend this quarter is genuinely positive on both fronts simultaneously
